intervals.note: No fetched source gives Wright Laboratory's founding date. Start is approximated to 2010, the earliest sourced HAYSTAC milestone (the experiment's INSPIRE date_proposed; see experiment:haystac intervals), used as a conservative lower bound for this open-ended 'active' interval (a hosted experiment cannot predate its host facility), not a claimed founding date. VERIFIER FIX (2026-09-17): an earlier fix used 2018 here, which the validator then flagged (experiment-before-facility) because HAYSTAC's own earliest interval starts in 2010; corrected to 2010 to resolve that inconsistency. The underlying issue this interval addresses is that the original start:null/end:null interval covered no date under A3, so the derived state at the build date was None while status said 'active' (validator error status-not-derived-state).
intervals.quote: Located at Yale's Wright Laboratory in New Haven, Connecticut, the HAYSTAC collaboration consists of members from Yale University, the University of California Berkeley, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and the University of Colorado at Boulder.

name: Yale Wright Laboratory
notes: No founding date for Wright Laboratory itself was sourced this session.

operator_text.quote: Located at Yale's Wright Laboratory in New Haven, Connecticut

summary.plain: Wright Laboratory is a Yale University physics building in New Haven, Connecticut. It hosts several fundamental-physics experiments, including HAYSTAC, which searches for the axion, a candidate particle for dark matter.
summary.technical: Yale University's nuclear/particle/astrophysics research building at 272 Whitney Avenue, New Haven, CT, host site of the HAYSTAC axion haloscope and other precision experiments.
